official_measurement_examples.name: Main river permit route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Work on or near a main river, flood defence, floodplain or sea defence can require an environmental permit.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ordinary watercourse distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Ordinary watercourses generally do not use the EA flood-risk permit route; local council or internal drainage board land-drainage consent may apply instead.

official_measurement_examples.name: Exemption condition
official_measurement_examples.fact: A flood-risk activity exemption must be registered and all exemption conditions must be met.

official_measurement_examples.name: Standard rules limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Standard-rules permits are only available where the activity fits the published criteria fully; otherwise a bespoke permit can be required.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning permission does not replace a required flood-risk activity permit or land-drainage consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ownership separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A permit does not establish riparian ownership, title or third-party access rights.

official_measurement_examples.name: Map limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Main-river mapping is a regulatory screening input and should not be treated as a surveyed bank or construction footprint boundary.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning flood assessment distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Flood-zone/FRA planning assessment and flood-risk activity permitting are separate tests with different purposes.

core_rules: main river and ordinary watercourse regimes remain distinct
flood-risk activity permit is not planning permission
planning permission is not flood-risk activity permit
bespoke permit need is activity and location specific
main-river map is screening not surveyed bank boundary
ordinary-watercourse consent authority may be council or IDB
riparian ownership is separate from permit status
permit does not grant third-party land access
permit does not prove flood safety of a development
flood-zone planning assessment is distinct from activity permitting
absence of main-river status is not absence of land-drainage controls
no parcel flood-permit clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
